# What SendGrid API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is, written out until each of the two segments is the length the
# pattern reads it at: twenty-two characters of identifier and forty-three of
# secret. Neither count is an abbreviation — a segment shortened for readability
# would leave a case holding no key at all — and their total with the prefix and
# the dot between them is the sixty-nine characters SendGrid states a key always
# is.
#
# The case under the over-match heading is not a key and nobody issued it. What
# it holds is a property chain whose first component closes on the prefix, whose
# second is exactly the length of an identifier and whose third is at least the
# length of a secret, which is the whole of what the pattern asks for.

patterns: sendgrid-api-key

# A key as it is written. One string serves every access level SendGrid issues,
# so what is below differs in where the key stands rather than in what kind it
# is: the create-key response it is first read out of, the bearer token header
# it is sent in, and the SMTP password SendGrid documents it being used as
# beside the username apikey.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       SENDGRID_API_KEY=SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SENDGRID_API_KEY=«sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a key in the response that first reports it
in:       {"api_key":"SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a","name":"My API Key"}
out:      {"api_key":"«sendgrid-api-key»","name":"My API Key"}

case:     a key in a bearer token header
in:       Authorization: Bearer SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      Authorization: Bearer «sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a key as the smtp password it doubles as
in:       smtp://apikey:SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a@smtp.sendgrid.net:587
out:      smtp://apikey:«sendgrid-api-key»@smtp.sendgrid.net:587

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a.
out:      the key is «sendgrid-api-key».

# The alphabet the two segments are written in: base64url, which is what the
# rulesets that spell a class admit behind the prefix, the hyphen and the
# underscore among them. Padding is not in it and does not arise: twenty-two
# and forty-three are the unpadded lengths of sixteen bytes and of thirty-two,
# and a padded encoding of the same bytes would not come to sixty-nine
# characters.

case:     a hyphen and an underscore in each segment
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef-1234_.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-123456789a
out:      «sendgrid-api-key»

case:     an equals sign where the secret ends
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789=
out:      SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789=

case:     a plus and a slash, which standard base64 writes where base64url writes - and _
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef+1234/.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SG.0123456789abcdef+1234/.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

# How long each segment is. Both counts are read exactly rather than as floors,
# which is where this pattern stands with the AWS, GitLab and Google ones rather
# than with the OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe, PyPI and npm ones: SendGrid states
# the length of a key itself, in a support article whose subject is that it
# never varies.
#
# So a segment of another length is not a key of another length. A run longer
# than a secret is a key with something written after it, and only the key is
# redacted; a segment shorter than its count — which is what a line cut to a
# column limit leaves — is no key at all, and every random character before the
# cut comes through in the clear. The cases below are both, and the second is
# here to be looked up rather than arrived at.

case:     an alphabet run longer than the secret
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      «sendgrid-api-key»b

case:     a secret one character short
in:       SENDGRID_API_KEY=SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789
out:      SENDGRID_API_KEY=SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789

case:     an identifier one character short
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef01234.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SG.0123456789abcdef01234.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     an identifier one character too long
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef0123456.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SG.0123456789abcdef0123456.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a key cut off at its prefix
in:       SENDGRID_API_KEY=SG.
out:      SENDGRID_API_KEY=SG.

# The dot between the two segments. It is the one character of the format that
# the alphabet does not hold, which is what ends a segment where it stands and
# what makes the count on either side of it readable at all. Nothing else
# divides the two.

case:     a hyphen where the separator belongs
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SG.0123456789abcdef012345-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     an underscore where the separator belongs
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SG.0123456789abcdef012345_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a space where the separator belongs
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SG.0123456789abcdef012345 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a plus at the first character of the identifier
in:       SG.+123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SG.+123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a second dot at the first character of the identifier
in:       SG..123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SG..123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a hyphen where the prefix carries its dot
in:       SG-0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SG-0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a further dot inside the secret
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef012345678.abcdef0123456789a
out:      SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef012345678.abcdef0123456789a

# What a key may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of a
# match, as there is none in any built-in but the Slack and Stripe ones: a
# demand in front would drop a key written against a letter rather than trim it,
# and one behind would drop a key with a character of its own alphabet after it.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       SENDGRID_API_KEY_SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SENDGRID_API_KEY_«sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xSG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      x«sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a key inside quotes
in:       export SENDGRID_API_KEY="SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a"
out:      export SENDGRID_API_KEY="«sendgrid-api-key»"

case:     a key before a hyphenated word
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a-suffix
out:      «sendgrid-api-key»-suffix

case:     a key between tabs
in:       \tSG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a\t
out:      \t«sendgrid-api-key»\t

case:     a key before a crlf
in:       SENDGRID_API_KEY=SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a\r\n
out:      SENDGRID_API_KEY=«sendgrid-api-key»\r\n

case:     a key in a markdown code span
in:       `SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a`
out:      `«sendgrid-api-key»`

case:     a key immediately against japanese on both sides
in:       キーはSG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789aです
out:      キーは«sendgrid-api-key»です

case:     a key against an invalid byte
in:       \xffSG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a\xff
out:      \xff«sendgrid-api-key»\xff

case:     a key cut short with an ellipsis
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123...
out:      SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123...

# Two keys written together. The prefix is two characters a segment is written
# with and the dot a key already carries between its segments, so a secret
# closing with SG opens a candidate two characters before its own key ends: the
# dot that candidate wants is the one written after the key, and a second key's
# identifier, dot and secret follow it. The two spans overlap and are redacted
# as one, which is what a scan resuming past a match would have stepped over.

case:     two keys separated by a space
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a SG.0123456789abcdef-1234_.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-123456789a
out:      «sendgrid-api-key» «sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a key written straight onto the end of another
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789aSG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sendgrid-api-key»«sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a key beginning inside the key before it
in:       SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012345678SG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sendgrid-api-key»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued, which is text somebody wrote:
# SG. can close an ordinary identifier — MSG., NSG., ESG. and PSG. each carry
# the whole prefix — so a property chain whose first component is one of them,
# whose second is exactly twenty-two characters of the alphabet and whose third
# is at least forty-three, is redacted from its SG onward.
#
# That is the answer rather than a fault in it: the chain from that SG is a
# key's format exactly, and the counts are already the vendor's own, so nothing
# is left in the string to read the two apart by. The tightening on offer is the
# one the Slack and Stripe patterns take, to ask that no letter and no digit
# stand in front of the prefix, and what it would cost is the case above where a
# key is written after a letter — which the pattern's own file weighs.

case:     a property chain whose first component closes on the prefix
in:       MSG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      M«sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a chain whose first component is NSG
in:       NSG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      N«sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a chain whose first component is ESG
in:       ESG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      E«sendgrid-api-key»

case:     a chain whose first component is PSG
in:       PSG.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      P«sendgrid-api-key»

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The prefix is read in its own case; a
# digest, a base64 payload and a base64url one each hold no dot and so no prefix
# to be found at, however long they run, and the last two of the three cases for
# that carry the two letters a prefix opens with and still hand it nowhere to
# close; no word of prose is spelled SG. with sixty-six characters of one run
# behind it; and a signed JWT is three dot-separated base64url segments as a key
# is and still carries no candidate — the header and the payload of one are
# JSON, so the bytes each encodes close with a brace, and base64url turns a
# final brace into 9, into 0 or into fQ, never into SG.

case:     a lowercase prefix
in:       sg.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      sg.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a value of the right shape opening with no prefix
in:       XY.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      XY.0123456789abcdef012345.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a hexadecimal digest
in:       sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a base64url payload carrying the letters a prefix opens with
in:       payload=SG0123456789abcdef012345SG0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      payload=SG0123456789abcdef012345SG0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     a base64 payload carrying them, written with the + and / base64url leaves out
in:       payload=SG0123456789abcdef+12345SG0123456789abcdef/123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      payload=SG0123456789abcdef+12345SG0123456789abcdef/123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef

case:     a log line
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="sending mail" url=https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/mail/send
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="sending mail" url=https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/mail/send
